svg.text: BASE - ALUMINIUM CORE, STAINLESS RIM RING, PORT FACE
the 60 (Cadrane) — desk dial
DRAWING
REV
SCALE
AS SHOWN
DATE
UNITS
mm

Projected from docs/v15/the60_v15_assembly.step by hidden-line projection, with dimension text written from docs/v15/the60_v15/src/params.py. No hand drafting. The knob is drawn on its turned profile: the knurl is on the part but is not drawn.
MODELLED, NOT MADE — no v15 part has been produced. Dimensions are model values, not inspection results. Bodies tagged ENVELOPE or ASSUMED in the model are drawn as envelopes, not as the real part.
SECTION D-D scale 1.75 : 1
Right half, on the 0 deg - 180 deg axis, through the port face. The base is three parts: the machined core, the ring round it and the closing plate under it.
CL
r 72.20 ducted core
r 75.20 ring bore
r 87.70 edge
NOTES
Rim ring, r 75.2 - 87.7 x 8.0 deep, machined stainless. stainless 304 or
316, bare. The outer wall r 84.0 - 87.7 carries the vent openings, 1.8 x
4.5 obround on a 120-position ring, each with a 0.3 x 45 deg polished
chamfer at the mouth; the parts list records 108 open once the ring screws
and the port slot have taken their share.
Core, r under 75.2, CNC 6082 aluminium: 2.0 web, 5.0 duct, ribs 6.0 tall
on the top face.
Closing plate: 1 mm laser-cut aluminium, r under 72.2, 9 x M2.5
countersunk from below, flush in the core's recess on a 0.2 gasket.
Unscrew it to clean the duct - it is the only way in.
Port face at r 79.7, 1.5 thick, carrying USB-C, a 3.5 mm jack, the barrel
jack and the ambient-light sensor looking rearward through a dia 4.8 hole.
The port slot through the core is 44.0 wide, from r 55.0 out to the rim.
The edge the user sees is the ring, not the core: the ring's outer face is
brushed axially and left bare, and every external face of the core is
black hard anodised. No masked pads anywhere - internal faces are chromate
or bare, so the finish line is a whole face, not a patch.
The ring is the mass at the largest radius and the structure the vents
pass through, so its section is set by the openings, not by stiffness.
Plate screws from below at 160 deg / 240 deg / 320 deg, into pillars on
the wall.
DETAIL S - RIM RING WALL 9 : 1
The openings pass through the 3.7 outer wall on 3 deg, into an underside
groove that the pad closes. The 0.8 undercut under the wall is what lets
the groove be machined without breaking through the visible face.
PLAN AT z 7.5 - THE CORE'S TOP FACE scale 0.55 : 1
0 deg
Three through-cuts: the Pi window, the carriage hole at 90 deg, the port slot at 0 deg.
Each keeps 2.5 of solid wall so the duct cannot leak into it. Ring bore r 75.2, duct ends r 72.2.
Ribs on this face stand 6.0 tall and carry the boards.
PLAN AT z 3.8 - THROUGH THE VENTS scale 0.55 : 1
The openings run all the way round except where the port slot and the ring's own
screw bosses interrupt them. Air crosses the inner land through 24 intake and
3 exhaust passages - that circuit is D05.
RIM RING - ISOMETRIC 0.50 : 1
The ring on its own, as machined. Every opening in the outer wall is on 3 deg to the radius, so the eye sees a fine louvre rather than a row of holes.
Finish: bare stainless - edge brushed axially, every opening mouth and both edges polished.
